newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May business inventories rose 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May business inventories rose 0.2 pct.

text.p: The Commerce Department said U.S. May business inventories rose 0.2 percent after rising a revised 0.4 percent in April. It said May business sales fell 0.5 percent after a revised 0.2 percent gain in April.
The following lists business inventories and sales by sector, in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted:
Wall Street economists had expected May business inventories to rise 0.3 percent.
The department said the 0.5 percent decline in May business sales was the biggest since June 1996 when they fell 0.7 percent.
The inventory-to-sales ratio is a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace.
The department revised April business inventories from up 0.3 percent. It also revised April business sales from a 0.3 percent rise.

The department issued revisions to April and May retail sales and April retail inventories on June 25. In that data it reported May retail sales at $210.16 billion and May auto sales at $50.55 billion.
